1a.topic: Packaging cost allocation using yield and box sizes
1a.note: No pre-exam source found; identical problem only appears later as SM May 2027 ed. Ch 2 Test Your Knowledge Q11 (post-exam, not counted).

1b.topic: Joint cost apportionment (sales value at split-off, by-product NRV credit) and further-processing decision
1b.note: Same structure as RTP Jan 2025 Q14 (JPBP Ltd: two joint products + by-product sold only after further processing, NRV deducted from joint cost, further processing/marketing costs, profit without processing, incremental decision); new figures and apportionment on sales value at split-off instead of physical units.

1c.topic: Halsey and Rowan premium plan earnings

sources.ref: SM Ch 3 Illustrations 6 and 7 (Halsey / Rowan earnings)

1c.note: PYQ May 2019 Q1(b) uses the same 40 hrs standard / 30 hrs actual for Halsey and Rowan; exam changes rate (150 vs 75), drops other plans and makes students derive standard time (1,800/45) and time taken from job start/finish times.

2a.topic: Cost sheet worked backwards from cost of production (FIFO finished stock)
2a.note: Backward derivation of raw material consumed as in PYQ Nov 2018 Q2(a) (ZIA Pvt Ltd); cost items (quality control, pollution control & maintenance, lease rent, primary packing) and the six-stage cost sheet follow PYQ May 2022 Q3(b); hire charges per labour hour, FIFO finished stock and new data are new.

2b.topic: Process account with normal/abnormal loss, container recovery and income statement
2b.note: No pre-exam source with this oil/container problem; identical problem only appears later as SM May 2027 ed. Ch 10 Test Your Knowledge Q8 (post-exam, not counted).

3a.topic: Service costing - bank loan application processing cost

sources.ref: SM Ch 12 Illustration 13 (home loan application processing)

3a.note: Same bank-branch set-up as PYQ Nov 2022 Q1(b) (ABC Bank: Vehicle/Education loans, branch manager, legal, printing, advertising, other expenses, equal processing cost); exam reverses the requirement (find direct professionals' salary), adds quarterly expenses and building depreciation, uses 20%/15% shares and new figures.

3b.topic: Service costing - training institute cost per batch, fee and break-even occupancy
3b.note: Same structure as PYQ Sep 2024 Q1(a) (Language Achievers: weekly hall rent, honorarium per lecture, travel per day, refreshments per week, admin expenses, cost per batch, minimum fee); exam changes data, adds weekend lectures and asks minimum % batch occupancy at a given fee instead of fee at 80% occupancy.

4a.topic: Material, labour and variable overhead variances from budget vs actual data

sources.ref: SM Ch 15 Test Your Knowledge Practical Problem Q6 (TQM Ltd.)

4a.note: Like SM Ch 15 TYK Q6, master budget vs actual units, sales, material, wages and VO with standard rates, from which material, labour and VO variances are worked; exam gives actual prices/rates (not actual quantities/hours) so quantities must be derived, all data new.

4b.topic: Cost sheet with absorption on normal capacity and cost-financial profit reconciliation

sources.ref: SM Ch 7 Test Your Knowledge Practical Problem Q4

4b.note: Same problem as SM Ch 7 TYK Q4 (normal capacity, no stock, DM/DW, factory expenses part fixed, fixed admin, S&D part fixed, interest & dividend income, cost sheet + reconciliation); figures and fixed % changed, admin expenses are unpaid production-related, financial P&L part dropped.

5a.topic: Comprehensive machine hour rate - working back to annual insurance premium

sources.ref: SM Ch 4 Test Your Knowledge Practical Problem Q5

5a.note: Same machine-shop problem as SM Ch 4 TYK Q5 (identical drilling machines, operators, absenteeism, leave, idle time, bonus, power, supervision, lighting, annual repairs/depreciation/sundry/general expenses); figures changed and requirement reversed: MHR of Rs 125 given, find annual insurance.

5b.topic: Capacity / activity ratios - working back actual and standard hours
5b.note: Same format as PYQ May 2024 Q1(c) (XYZ Ltd.: std hours/day, days/week, 4 weeks, max and actual employees, two ratios given, find actual hours, standard hours and other ratios); exam gives Actual Capacity Usage and Activity ratios instead of Actual Usage of Budgeted Capacity and Efficiency, new figures.

5c.note: Same wording and layout as SM Ch 14 Illustration 10 (make any one of the products, option at beginning of year, SP, VC, demand, capacity, fixed cost, compute opportunity cost); two products M and S instead of three, new figures.

6a.chapter: 1 Introduction to Cost and Management Accounting

sources.ref: SM Ch 1 Classification of Costs: 13.2 By Function and 13.3 By Variability or Behaviour
SM Ch 4 Classification of overheads by function (table: delivery van expenses, warehouse expenses, salesmen commission)

6a.note: Application of the SM Ch 1 functional and variability classifications (and SM Ch 4 functional overhead table) to five items; no earlier paper asks this exact item list, RTP Nov 2022 Q15(a) is a similar classify-into-table format (direct/indirect, fixed/variable).

6b.topic: Suitable incentive scheme (Rowan) for stated management requirements
6b.note: Word-for-word the three conditions of SM Ch 3 Illustration 11 (answer: Rowan scheme); only the numerical demonstration requirement is dropped.

sources.ref: SM Ch 15 para 5.8 Components of Budgetary Control System (also TYK Theoretical Q2)

sources.ref: SM Ch 14 Test Your Knowledge Practical Problem Q20 (Prisha Ltd.)

m2.note: Profit for existing mix as asked in RTP May 2022 Q12(i); SM TYK Q20 asks only C/S and BES. New figures.

sources.ref: SM Ch 14 Test Your Knowledge Practical Problem Q20(ii)

m3.note: Proposed-mix C/S ratio after replacing a product, as in RTP May 2022 Q12(ii) and SM TYK Q20(ii); new figures.

m4.topic: Multi-product CVP: break-even sales at proposed mix

sources.ref: SM Ch 14 Test Your Knowledge Practical Problem Q20(ii)

m4.note: Break-even sales for proposed mix as in RTP May 2022 Q12(ii)/SM TYK Q20(ii); exam also raises fixed cost in proposal (18.8 lakh vs 18 lakh).

m5.topic: Multi-product CVP: profit at proposed mix

sources.ref: SM Ch 14 Test Your Knowledge Practical Problem Q20 (Prisha Ltd.)

m5.note: Profit for proposed mix as in RTP May 2022 Q12(ii); new figures.

m6.topic: Annual raw material requirement from market demand and market share
m6.note: Case Scenario II opening ('manufactures X used by ...; total market demand; expected market share %') follows the EBQ problems of MTP Nov 2018 S-II Q4(b), RTP Nov 2020 Q7, PYQ Jan 2021 Q1(d); exam uses quarterly demand and converts to kg of two raw materials.

m7.topic: EOQ with carrying cost built from storage and interest rates
m7.note: Carrying cost built up from storage and interest components as in SM Ch 2 Illustration 4; exam states them per kg per month and per quarter so they must be annualised; new data.

m8.topic: EOQ and number of orders (storage + interest + obsolescence rates)
m8.note: Same carrying-cost structure as SM Ch 2 Illustration 4 (storage, interest, obsolescence % per annum of price) plus number of orders (Illustration 3); new figures.

m9.topic: Total annual inventory cost at EOQ
m9.note: Total cost = purchase + ordering + carrying at EOQ exactly as in SM Ch 2 Illustration 4(i); new figures.

m10.topic: Total annual inventory cost at a non-EOQ order size
m10.note: Total cost computation of SM Ch 2 Illustration 4 applied to a policy order size of 200 kg (cf. cost at a policy run size in PYQ Jan 2021 Q1(d)(iii)); new data.

m11.topic: Labour rate variance - actual wage rate per unit

sources.ref: Model Test Paper 1 Q3 (Part I MCQ)

m11.note: Identical to Model Test Paper 1 MCQ 3 (30 minutes/unit, Rs 50/hr, 30,000 units, LRV 7,500 A, LEV nil, same four options); only 'repair time' reworded to 'production time'.

m12.topic: Reverse calculation of factory overhead recovery rate on a job

sources.ref: SM Ch 4 Illustration 9 (Reverse calculation of factory and administrative overheads)

m12.note: Same reverse working as PYQ May 2022 Q2(a) / SM Ch 4 Illustration 9 (factory OH % of direct wages, admin OH % of factory cost, profit % on total cost); exam gives one job with admin rate known (25%) so only the factory OH rate is solved; new figures.

m13.topic: Labour hours and number of operators required for a production target
m13.note: Simple hours/operators computation (480 dozen x 15 min = 1,440 hrs; 36 operators); no comparable question found in pre-exam SM/RTP/MTP/PYQ.

m14.note: Same layout as SM Ch 2 Illustration 13 (opening stock, dated purchases and issues, value consumed under LIFO); exam has one issue and new figures.

m15.topic: Revised spare parts cost for machine hour rate (price and consumption increase)
m15.note: Spare-parts adjustment of the machine-hour-rate problem in RTP Nov 2020 Q3 (spare parts Rs 1,00,000 = 40,000 + 40,000 + 20,000; +15% price; +25% consumption for B & C); exam merges the 60,000 into machine B and asks only this element.
